[disputes-unauthorized] Disputing a transaction you didn't make (effective 2026-01-15)
If you see a card transaction you didn't make or authorize, you can dispute it as unauthorized.

## First, protect your card

Before we open an unauthorized dispute, the card used must be frozen or reported lost or stolen. That stops more charges while we investigate. If the card is still in your wallet, freezing is enough.

## How long you have

Report an unauthorized transaction within 60 days of the date of the statement it first appeared on. Statements close on the last calendar day of each month. For example, a transaction that posted in March appears on the

[disputes-unauthorized] Disputing a transaction you didn't make (effective 2026-01-15)
window.

## Not sure it's unauthorized?

Unfamiliar names are often a merchant's parent company or a payment processor. Tap the transaction to see the merchant's details before you dispute it.

Questions? Our support team is available in the app at any hour.

you don't recognize at all are a different kind of dispute. See "Disputing a transaction you didn't make".

Need more help? Message us in the app any time, day or night.

[disputes-merchant-v2] Disputing a purchase with a merchant (effective 2026-01-15)
If you paid for something with your card and there's a problem with the purchase itself, you can file a merchant dispute. This covers:

- Items or services you paid for but never received
- Items that were significantly different from what was described
- Subscriptions or recurring charges that continued after you cancelled

## Contact the merchant first

Before you dispute, try to sort it out with the merchant, and keep a record of what you sent and what they said. We'll ask for it.

[disputes-duplicate] Charged twice for the same thing (effective 2025-01-01)
Seeing the same charge twice doesn't always mean you were charged twice.

## Check if one is pending

Hotels, gas stations, car rentals and restaurants often place a temporary authorization, then post the final amount separately. The pending one usually drops off within 7 days. Pending transactions can't be disputed.

## If both have posted

If two identical charges have both posted, contact the merchant first. Most will refund a duplicate quickly. If the merchant doesn't help, dispute the second charge in the app as a duplicate. Tap the transaction, then Get help, then Charged

[disputes-pending] Why can't I dispute a pending transaction? (effective 2025-01-01)
any more charges. When the transaction posts, dispute it as unauthorized. Your dispute window starts from the statement it posts on, so you won't lose time by waiting.

## If the amount is wrong

Pending amounts are often estimates, for example at gas pumps or hotels. The posted amount is usually different. Wait and see what posts.

## If it's been pending a long time

Some merchants take longer. If a transaction has been pending much longer than usual, message support and we'll look at it.
